text: dsh-window-size-keeper 是面向 DSH 桌面端的窗口尺寸恢复插件。它在 Windows 上记录主窗口外框尺寸并在下次启动时恢复；设置页提供常用分辨率、自定义宽高和居中选项，选择后立即应用并保存。它也会记录手动调整的尺寸供下次启动使用。无需 API 密钥或外部服务，适合固定桌面布局。

dsh-window-size-keeper remembers DSH desktop window size. On Windows it restores the main window after restart. Its settings section offers preset or custom dimensions, centering, and immediate apply. Manual resizing can become the next startup size. No API key or external service is needed.
我想让 DSH 下次启动时保留上次调整的窗口大小。
能不能给 DSH 桌面版设置一个固定分辨率？
我想从设置页直接改主窗口宽高并马上生效。
DSH 每次启动尺寸都回到默认值，怎么记住自定义尺寸？
帮我把 DSH 窗口居中，并在以后启动时恢复尺寸。
How can I keep my DSH desktop window size after restarting?
I want to choose a custom resolution for the DSH main window.
Can DSH remember the size I manually resize its window to?
dsh-window-size-keeper 的功能「启动恢复」：Windows 上启动时读取主窗口的已保存尺寸，尽早调整并可居中。
dsh-window-size-keeper 的功能「窗口大小设置」：设置页可选预设或输入宽高、切换居中；提交后立即调整窗口并保存。
dsh-window-size-keeper feature “Remember resizing”: detected manual size changes are saved for the next startup.
dsh-window-size-keeper 只在 Windows 上实际调整窗口；其他平台的设置只记录而不应用。状态和设置保存在本机 DSH storage 目录。
dsh-window-size-keeper uses Windows APIs. It compiles and stores a local helper by default, with PowerShell as fallback.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · The problem：DSH desktop (Electron) rebuilds its main window at a fixed default size (1280×820) on every start, so the size you resized to last time is lost. This plugin records the main window's last **outer frame** (title bar and borders included, in physical pixels), restores and centres it on the next start, and adds a **Window size** section to the DSH settings page where you can pick 1920×1080, 1280×720 and other common resolutions, or any custom width×height.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · The “Window size” settings section (added 2026-10-11)：DSH desktop → Settings → **Window size** (the same level as the Plugins and Desk pet sections, `order: 65`). What's in it:

dsh-window-size-keeper README · The “Window size” settings section (added 2026-10-11)：| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Restore size radio group | "Last size" (default) / 12 common resolutions / "Custom…" |
| Custom width & height inputs | any size (outer frame, physical pixels) via "Apply custom size" |
| Centre on restore switch | centres on the primary work area; off = resize only, position untouched |
| Apply current selection | re-runs one resize with the current selection, changing nothing |
| Current outer frame / next-start size / file paths | status read-out |

dsh-window-size-keeper README · The “Window size” settings section (added 2026-10-11)：**When it takes effect:** immediately — picking a value resizes the main window at once (centring per your setting) and writes it to the settings file, so the next start uses the same size.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · The “Window size” settings section (added 2026-10-11)：About the numbers: every value is the **outer frame** (title bar + borders) in **physical pixels**, identical to what `GetWindowRect` returns. With DPI scaling above 100% the same numbers look smaller than they read (1920×1080 does not fit a 1920-wide screen at 125% scaling and gets clamped to the work area), which is why the list includes `1536×864` (= 1920×1080 at 125% scaling).

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Display language (added 2026-10-19)：| # | Source | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `language` in patch config (delivered to the page through `GET /state`) | `"zh"` / `"en"` pins the language. Anything unrecognised — including `zh-TW` — is not treated as "pinned Chinese" and falls through |
| 2 | The DSH client's active language (`ctx.locale`, i.e. Settings → General → Language) | follows whatever you selected in DSH, **switching languages takes effect at once** — no reload, no restart, and no rebuild of the section (text already typed into the custom width/height boxes survives the switch) |
| 3 | The plugin's own detection (`navigator` / `Intl`) | used only when the client runtime provides no language service (DSH 0.1.x clients). **Only Simplified Chinese counts as Chinese**: `zh`, `zh-Hans*`, `zh-CN`, `zh-SG`, `zh-MY`; `zh-TW` / `zh-HK` / `zh-MO` / `zh-Hant*` and every other language get English |

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Display language (added 2026-10-19)：The host half does no UI translation. It ships data plus stable machine-readable reasons: failure `code`s (rendered per language by the client), validation `noteCodes`, and both alias spellings of every preset (`label` / `labelEn`). If a preset you defined in patch config has no `labelEn`, it is displayed exactly as you wrote it — your own names are never machine-translated.

Two deliberate choices:

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Display language (added 2026-10-19)：- **`"locale"` is deliberately *not* declared in the client module's `inject`.** Declaring a service the runtime doesn't provide drops this half of the plugin entirely — the section just disappears, without an error. The language service only exists on DSH 0.2 clients, so `ctx.locale` is read optionally and wrapped in try/catch; without it the plugin falls back to rule 3 and nothing else degrades.
- **Unrecognised error codes never reach the user as codes.** Known codes are rendered from the dictionary; an unknown code falls back to whatever text the host supplied, and only if that is missing too does it show a generic failure line.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · How it works：- The host process (DSH host, a child of the Electron main process) **starts watching the main window at `apply` time**: it keeps a resident Win32 agent - first choice a small helper exe compiled on the user's own machine, `powershell.exe` as fallback - that enumerates windows every 40 ms and acts the moment the main window appears. Identification rule: host parent PID + `Chrome_WidgetWin_1` window class + outer-frame area ≥ `earlyMinArea`. While watching, the window is still **hidden** and its title has not become the product name yet, so this stage identifies windows by area (which keeps the 600×700 welcome window and the 720×760 login window out); when two candidates have similar areas it declares "can't tell" and looks again next round — it never guesses.
- **Why that yields "opens at last time's size":** the desktop app creates its main window **hidden → `loadURL` → `show()`** (`createWindow(appPreload, false, true)` and `enterWorkspace` in `lib/main.js`), and Electron only creates it after the host reports `ready`. So there is a window of time where the main window exists but isn't visible, and the agent finishes resizing inside it

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Sampling cadence and following a manual resize (added 2026-10-20)：- **Cadence is adaptive, not fixed.** Idle: read the outer frame every `saveIntervalMs` (15 s). The moment a sample differs from the previous one (size or position), the next reads switch to `activeSampleMs` (1 s) and keep that pace until `activeTailMs` (10 s) has passed since the last observed change. All three keys accept positive numbers only - 0, negatives and garbage fall back to the defaults, and the floors (1 s idle, 250 ms fast) keep a typo from turning into a 0 ms busy loop.
- **Why it matters:** the state file and the "current outer frame" line on the settings page are only as fresh as the last sample, and the exit hook flushes that same cache. With the old fixed 15 s poll, resizing and immediately restarting DSH lost that resize - the next start went back to the size before it. The adaptive chain bounds the damage to about a second while idle cost stays exactly as before.
- **`followManualResize` (on by default): a manual resize also updates your selection.** When a sample shows the *width or height* changed, the plugin writes `settings.json` itself and the "Restore size" se

dsh-window-size-keeper README · State and settings files：| File | Written by | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state.json` | plugin polling / exit backstop | `{ "version": 1, "width": 1894, "height": 1171, "x": 18, "y": 17, "savedAt": "..." }` (outer frame, physical pixels) |
| `settings.json` | settings page; also written by the plugin itself when it adopts a manual resize (`followManualResize`) | `{ "version": 1, "preset": "1920x1080", "centerOnRestore": true, "custom": { "width": 1600, "height": 1000 }, "updatedAt": "..." }`; `preset` empty = use "last size", `"custom"` = use the `custom` width/height |
| `state.json.gen` | plugin | generation counter (bumped per apply, for hot-reload zombie protection); never maintained by hand |
| `wsk-agent-<16 hex of source>.exe` + the matching `.cs` | plugin (compiled the first time Win32 is needed, reused afterwards) | the Win32 helper: the C# source ships in the package, the compilation happens only on your machine, and the `.cs` sits next to the exe so you can read what is running. Changing the source retires the cache by itself. Set `win32Backend: "powershell"` if you would rather no exe were ever written here; deleting these two file

dsh-window-size-keeper README · State and settings files：Both JSON files are written **atomically** (temp file + rename) so a concurrent reader can't catch a half-written file.

Deleting `state.json` resets "last size"; deleting `settings.json` returns the settings page to its default (use "last size").

dsh-window-size-keeper README · HTTP routes (the channel between the settings page and the host)：Prefix `/window-size-keeper/api` (registered through the host's `webServer.register({ kind: "prefix" })`; `webServer` is not in `inject`, so headless setups don't hard-depend on it, and registration retries a bounded number of times if the service arrives late).

dsh-window-size-keeper README · HTTP routes (the channel between the settings page and the host)：| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /state` | available resolutions, current selection, most recent window rectangle, bounds, both file paths, and which Win32 layer is actually in use (`win32Backend`, `win32HelperExe`) |
| `POST /select` | `{ preset, custom:{width,height}, centerOnRestore }` → validate + persist + apply at once |
| `POST /apply` | apply the current selection once (resize + centre) |
| `POST /reset` | selection back to "last size" (`preset: ""`) and apply |

text: dsh-window-size-keeper README · HTTP routes (the channel between the settings page and the host)：Invalid input (unknown `preset` id, custom width/height that aren't positive integers, picking “Custom…” without ever entering a size) is rejected with a reason — never silently applied.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Configuration (cordis.patch.yml)：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | master switch (off also stops registering the settings routes) |
| `saveIntervalMs` | `15000` | idle sampling interval: how often the frame is read while nothing is changing |
| `activeSampleMs` | `1000` | sampling interval while a change is in flight (floor 250 ms) |
| `activeTailMs` | `10000` | how long after the last observed change fast sampling continues |
| `followManualResize` | `true` | when a manual width/height change is sampled, set the "Restore size" selection to `custom` = that size (see the section above) |
| `restoreDelayMs` | `3000` | first-restore delay on the fallback path (only used when `restoreEarly` is off or nothing was found) |
| `restoreEarly` | `true` | early restore: watch from `apply` and fix the size before `show()`. Off restores the pure-polling behaviour |
| `earlyPollMs` | `40` | interval between enumerations inside the agent while watching |
| `earlyBudgetMs` | `10000` | total early-restore budget; on expiry it hands over to `restoreDelayMs` |
| `earlyMinArea` | `900000` | minimum outer-frame area (physical px²) acc

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Configuration (cordis.patch.yml)：> Note: `preset`/`presets` belong to the Cordis patch config and need a **DSH restart** (or a profile reassembly) to take effect; `dev_reload_package` does not re-read patch config. Selections made on the settings page go through `settings.json` and need **no** restart.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Presets：To add or remove entries, put a `presets:` list in `config` of `cordis.patch.yml` (each item `{ id, label, labelEn?, width, height }`), which replaces the built-in list wholesale (example in the trailing comment of `cordis.patch.yml`); the settings-page list follows it. `labelEn` is optional — omit it and that entry shows the same text in both languages.

dev_reload_package   dsh-window-size-keeper   # swaps the host half only; the settings page still needs a reload

Uninstall: `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-window-size-keeper`, or `dev_uninject_plugin dsh-window-size-keeper`.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · development: hot-assemble (no restart)：> What goes into `<profile>`? Usually `desktop` for the desktop app and `web` for the web app, but the name is decided by your machine: `dir %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles` (Linux/macOS: `ls ~/.dsh/profiles`). A wrong name doesn't error — the plugin just lands in a different profile and you won't see it here.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · development: hot-assemble (no restart)：> **After adding or changing `lib/client.js`** (the settings-page half): the client half is loaded by the page, so a profile reassembly (restart the DSH desktop app) plus a page refresh is needed before a new section appears. Changes to the host half (`lib/index.js`) can be hot-reloaded with `dev_reload_package`.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Offline self-check：```bash
node scripts/selftest.mjs                                    # or npm test
node --check lib/index.js && node --check lib/client.js      # or npm run check
```

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Offline self-check：`scripts/selftest.mjs` is dependency-free and covers 99 checks across thirteen labelled groups (0.1.1 added group `[5c]` - the sampling cadence and the "was this resize manual?" decision as pure functions - plus a render check that the frame line shows the real size after a refresh and after a language switch; 0.1.3 added group `[7b]` - the Win32 helper's path-picking pure functions, a real compile on the machine running the test, the three one-shot contracts and the resident protocol, and "if the helper cannot start we must fall back to powershell, never give up"): the pure functions (centring, clamping, priority, input validation, main-window identification, settings/state read-write), the HTTP routes (fake ctx + real http server + real fetch), the Win32 agent protocol against a real `powershell.exe` **and** against the locally compiled helper exe, the i18n dictionaries (key parity, identical `{placeholders}`, no untranslated leftovers in the English table, language resolution priority), and rendering the actual section into a fake DOM in both languages — including "switching language must not rebuild the DOM, so the custom width

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Offline self-check：Group [10] is a desensitization scan (`scripts/check-sensitive.mjs`, runnable on its own as `npm run scan:sensitive`): it refuses account home directories (`C:\Users\<someone>`, `/home/<someone>`), personal workspace absolute paths, hard-coded loopback ports, credential-shaped strings (`api_key: …`, `ghp_…`, `sk-…`, `AKIA…`), real e-mail addresses and machine fingerprints (SID / machine GUID / hostname) anywhere in the shipped files or the repo-only release docs. It carries its own must-be-red and must-be-green control samples — the scanner prints how many at run time and selftest group [10] enforces both halves — so the gate cannot quietly rot into a rubber stamp; `~/.dsh`, `%USERPROFILE%`, `<workspace>` and `<HOME>` plus SHA-256 digests are deliberately allowed — a ledger that cannot write down a checksum is not much of a ledger.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · Offline self-check：It points the state and settings files at a temporary directory, and the helper exe it compiles during the test lands in that same temporary directory - it **never touches** the real `~/.dsh/storages/window-size-keeper`. The script's parent process is not the DSH host, so `applyNow` inside the routes can't find a main window — which is exactly what proves failures are reported honestly instead of being claimed as done, and no real window gets resized. To verify on the real machine: restart the desktop app and look at Settings → Window size.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · The zero-dependency red line：Node builtins + the in-box `csc.exe` (to compile the Win32 helper) + `powershell.exe` (fallback) only; no runtime dependency is declared, **and the package ships no binary at all** - the helper exe is compiled on the user's own machine from C# source that is part of the package. The rule holds in either install mode: when a profile installs the packaged tarball, any declared runtime dependency would have to resolve from the registry during install, and when a profile links this directory for development (pnpm `link:`) pnpm does not install the linked package's own dependencies at all - either way an unresolvable runtime dependency makes the whole Cordis plugin tree throw and DSH cannot start (the 2026-09 incident; the same warning is in `@dsh-pet/bridge`). The client half follows the same rule: it only uses the `react` the client module loader already injects, and no third-party package.

dsh-window-size-keeper README · What lives where on a machine：`<workspace>/dsh-window-size-keeper` is the one checkout: code, both READMEs, both changelogs, the release ledger, `PUBLISHING.md`, the market submission entry, CI and `.git`. Version identity is the annotated tag `v<version>` - the old habit of keeping a second directory named `<name>-<version>` as a release snapshot was retired on 2026-10-20 and nothing depends on it. `<workspace>` stands for "wherever this checkout lives on your machine" — the repo deliberately records no absolute paths from anyone's machine, and a selftest group enforces that. What DSH actually runs is a packaged artifact rather than this directory: `npm pack` writes `dist/<name>-<version>.tgz` and the profile installs it from `~/.dsh/.plugin-sources/<name>-<version>.tgz`, so editing `lib/*.js` here takes effect only after pack + `dsh plugin … add` + a full DSH restart (or a temporary `link:` while debugging). Everything the plugin writes at runtime lives in `~/.dsh/storages/window-size-keeper/`: `state.json`, `settings.json`, `state.json.gen`, plus the compiled `wsk-agent-*.exe` and its `.cs` (deleting those only means recompiling next time, and del
